source: twelve relations of the second confirmatory batch, specified from publisher documentation (e3/truth/docs/fresh2/) by three subagents that never saw data, mined FDs or model answers; parts A (benchmarks), B (ChEMBL, MusicBrainz, PLUTO, FHRS), C (GeoNames, EIA-860, STATS19, GHCN)
rule: part A: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. For the three BenchBase benchmarks the DDL at the pinned commit is the specification of the generated data (scale factor 1); a dependency that the H-Store project page states and the DDL neither declares nor contradicts is ambiguous and is recorded with sure: false, quoting both. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part B: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, unique constraint on a NOT NULL column, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or containment statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out, when two documents conflict, or when a unique index covers a nullable column. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state, and documented non-dependencies, are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened. | part C: Sigma* is the set of FDs that the publisher documentation implies among the attributes of each relation, projected and closed over the dropped columns, each with a verbatim quote; sure when the quoted text states it (declared key, foreign key to a declared key, an explicit one-to-one or nesting statement), unsure when it needs an inference the text does not spell out. Dependencies the documentation hints at but does not state are listed under undocumented_regularities and are not part of Sigma*. Written from the documentation alone, before any data file was opened.

instance.generator: public data fixed before download for the second confirmatory evaluation, converted by unpack_fresh2.py and joined by fresh.py
instance.construction: Wikimedia SQL table dumps of simplewiki, run 20261001 (dumps.wikimedia.org/simplewiki/20261001/, status 'Dump complete'): simplewiki-20261001-categorylinks.sql.gz (27.2 MB, sha1 99c462640edea0d1b853dbae5a120417ab57280a), simplewiki-20261001-page.sql.gz (31.2 MB, sha1 765d7db75eeb964da5017d970258785b9cfec5d9) and simplewiki-20261001-linktarget.sql.gz (36.1 MB, sha1 1f3017c5224875d1edf23dc35f38bbd9317d65bd), each converted to mediawiki/<table>.csv with the column names of the dump's CREATE TABLE, which for the MediaWiki 1.47.0-wmf.24 that simple.wikipedia.org runs (Special:Version, 2026-10-28) is the 1.45+ layout of tables-generated.sql at the pinned commit (categorylinks with cl_target_id and without cl_to): categorylinks (root; sampled to 1,000,000 records if larger) left-joined to page on cl_from = page_id and to linktarget on cl_target_id = lt_id; no column dropped except page_id and lt_id, which equal the join columns; page_title, lt_title, cl_sortkey and cl_sortkey_prefix are binary columns and are written as the dump's byte strings decoded as UTF-8 where valid.

cleaning.missing_values: empty and missing references become '?', kept as a value (null = null)

truth.clause: mediawiki_tables.json, categorylinks.cl_type comment: "Stores whether cl_from is a category, file, or other page, so we can paginate the three categories separately. This only has to be updated when moving pages into or out of the category namespace, since file pages cannot be moved to other namespaces, nor can non-files be moved into the file namespace."; mediawiki_Manual_Categorylinks_table.wiki, cl_type: "What type of page is this (file, subcat (subcategory) or page (normal page))."
truth.justification: Unsure: cl_type classifies the member page as a category page, a file page or another page, which is decided by the page's namespace, and the comment ties its maintenance to namespace moves; but no text says cl_type is a function of page_namespace, and a row is refreshed only when the page is re-parsed after a move, so rows may lag.

audit.quote: Stores whether cl_from is a category, file, or other page, so we can paginate the three categories separately. This only has to be updated when moving pages into or out of the category namespace, since file pages cannot be moved to other namespaces, nor can non-files be moved into the file namespace. ‖ What type of page is this (file, subcat (subcategory) or page (normal page)). ‖ Stores the time at which that link was last updated in the table. ‖ 2026-10-01 21:33:50 done Wiki category membership link records. ‖ 2026-10-01 21:35:02 done Base per-page data (id, title, old restrictions, etc).

truth.clause: mediawiki_tables.json, categorylinks.cl_sortkey comment: "A binary string obtained by applying a sortkey generation algorithm (Collation::getSortKey()) to page_title, or cl_sortkey_prefix . "\n" page_title if cl_sortkey_prefix is nonempty."; mediawiki_tables.json, categorylinks.cl_collation_id comment: "FK to collation_id"; mediawiki_Manual_Categorylinks_table.wiki, cl_sortkey: "This is the binary sortkey, that depending on {{ll|manual:$wgCategoryCollation|$wgCategoryCollation}} may or may not be readable by a human"; mediawiki_Manual_Categorylinks_table.wiki, cl_sortkey_prefix: "Otherwise it is the human readable version of the first part of cl_sortkey."
truth.justification: Unsure: the sortkey is computed from the prefix and the member page's title under the collation that cl_collation_id records, so the three determine it for a current row; the text describes a computation rather than stating a constraint, the sortkey is truncated to 230 bytes, and a row whose page was renamed keeps its old sortkey until the page is re-parsed.

audit.quote: A binary string obtained by applying a sortkey generation algorithm (Collation::getSortKey()) to page_title, or cl_sortkey_prefix . \"\\n\" page_title if cl_sortkey_prefix is nonempty. ‖ If nonempty, it's concatenated with a line break followed by the page title before the sortkey conversion algorithm is run. We store this so that we can update collations without reparsing all pages. ‖ Used so that if the [[Special:MyLanguage/Manual:$wgCategoryCollation|collation changes]], the {{ll|Manual:updateCollation.php|updateCollation.php}} script knows what rows need to be fixed in db. ‖ Needed mostly so that cl_sortkey can be easily updated in certain situations without re-parsing the entire page. ‖ Stores the time at which that link was last updated in the table.
